title: Medical Research Must Address Humanity’s Healthcare Challenges: Vice-President at Dr. NTR University’s Ruby Jubilee
subtitle:
“Dr. NTR, a Legend of India, Was a Leader Who Thought Beyond Regional Boundaries”: Vice-President

Technology Must Serve Humanity; Compassion Remains at the Heart of Healthcare: Vice-President

Doctors Must Lead Society’s Fight Against Drug Abuse: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 2:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today called upon medical institutions to strengthen research, foster innovation and develop solutions to pressing healthcare challenges, while addressing the 40th (Ruby Jubilee) Anniversary Celebrations of Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Ruby Jubilee celebrations of Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences in Vijayawada today.

He called upon medical institutions to strengthen research and innovation to address humanity’s healthcare challenges, emphasising that technology must serve humanity and compassion remain at the heart of healthcare.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 26, 2026
Congratulating the University on completing four decades of service to medical education and healthcare, the Vice-President said that the institution embodies the vision of former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and legendary leader Dr. Nandamuri Taraka Rama Rao. He noted that Dr. NTR’s vision and public service extended beyond regional boundaries, reflecting a broader commitment to the welfare of the nation.
Highlighting the expansion of medical education under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President said that the number of medical colleges in India has more than doubled, from 387 before 2014 to 846 at present. MBBS seats have increased by 172 per cent, from around 51,000 to over 1.4 lakh, while postgraduate seats have risen by 177 per cent, from around 31,000 to over 86,000.
Emphasising that the next frontier must be research and innovation, the Vice-President urged talented students to dedicate themselves to addressing healthcare challenges facing humanity. He expressed hope that researchers from Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences would achieve global recognition, including the Nobel Prize, through their contributions to medical science.
Observing that Artificial Intelligence, digital health, telemedicine and advanced diagnostic technologies are transforming healthcare, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan encouraged the University to establish collaborations with leading universities to provide students and researchers greater exposure to advanced research and emerging technologies. He stressed that technological progress must be guided by scientific validation, patient safety, data privacy and ethical responsibility, adding that technology cannot replace the compassion and human connection central to the doctor-patient relationship.
The Vice-President also called upon doctors and healthcare professionals to play a proactive role in creating awareness against drug abuse. Describing the fight against drugs as a collective responsibility, he urged the medical fraternity to lead efforts to build a drug-free society.
As part of the programme, the Vice-President joined the gathering in taking a pledge to say no to drugs and promote a drug-free society.He also released a souvenir commemorating the University’s 40-year journey.
Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Chancellor of the University; Shri Kolusu Parthasarathy, Minister for Housing, Information and Public Relations, Government of Andhra Pradesh; Dr. P. Chandrasekhar, Vice-Chancellor of the University; Dr. M. K. Ramesh, President of the Medical Assessment and Rating Board, National Medical Commission, and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.
Earlier on his arrival at Vijaywada airport, Vice President Shri C P Radhakrishnan was warmly received by Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Shri Nara Lokesh, Cabinet Minister , Govt. of Andhra Pradesh and other dignitaries.

title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER URGES BRICS PARLIAMENTS TO CHAMPION ETHICAL, RESPONSIBLE, AND TRANSPARENT TECHNOLOGY WITH PARAMOUNT HUMAN OVERSIGHT
subtitle:
INDIA DEMONSTRATES PIONEERING DIGITAL INITIATIVES INCLUDING DIGITAL SANSAD, NEVA, AND MULTILINGUAL PLATFORMS TO BOOST TRANSPARENCY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER HOLDS BILATERAL ENGAGEMENTS WITH DELEGATIONS FROM THE UAE, CHINA, AND IRAN ON THE SIDELINES OF THE FORUM

INDIA AND CHINA HAVE A SHARED RESPONSIBILITY TO MAINTAIN PEACE AND TRANQUILLITY ALONG THE BORDER: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 10:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today urged BRICS Parliaments to champion ethical, responsible and transparent technology with paramount human oversight.
Addressing the Plenary Sessions, as part of the ongoing 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum, Shri Birla said, BRICS nations representing approximately half of the world's population, share a collective responsibility to use technology ethically while safeguarding parliamentary sovereignty and fostering mutual cooperation.
Earlier in the day, Shri Birla inaugurated the forum.
Shri Birla outlined several digital innovations introduced by the Parliament of India to improve legislative capacity, transparency, efficiency, and public access, which include secure digital platforms providing MPs with online access to questions, answers, and prompt government department responses; multilingual initiatives offering the daily List of Business in 10 languages - with ongoing work toward all 22 scheduled languages - and simultaneous interpretation in 22 languages.
He also highlighted archival digitization of pre - and post-independence parliamentary debates equipped with metadata and video-search facilities; 24/7 online access to research papers alongside home delivery of books from the Parliament Library; and paperless governance initiatives utilizing the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) and the 'One Nation, One Legislative Platform' to connect legislatures and enable live streaming of proceedings, debates, budgets, and law-making information.
Shri Birla spoke about India's globally recognized Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), which empowers citizens, promotes financial inclusion, and ensures transparent benefit transfers directly to bank accounts to reduce corruption. Stressing that technology must be responsible, accountable, and human-centric, he noted that advanced technology must align with human sensitivities, ethical values, and dignity, keeping human oversight paramount.
On the sidelines of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026, Shri Birla hosted H.E. Mr. Saqr Ghobash, Speaker of the Federal National Council of the UAE. The two leaders reaffirmed historic bonds of friendship and committed to enhancing parliamentary cooperation through regular dialogue, delegation exchanges, and sharing best practices in digital governance via Digital Sansad, Artificial Intelligence, committee functioning, and the Online Assurance Monitoring System. Aligning with the shared aspirations of Viksit Bharat and We the UAE 2031, they discussed expanding ties in trade, investment, education, youth exchanges, and people-to-people connections, while emphasizing regional peace and stability through diplomacy.
Later, Shri Birla met Hon. Zheng Jianbang, Vice Chairman of the National People’s Congress of the People’s Republic of China. The two leaders discussed strengthening India-China relations through parliamentary exchanges, regular dialogue, and cooperation in areas such as education, healthcare, and technology. Shri Birla emphasized that as neighbors, both countries have a shared responsibility to maintain peace and tranquillity along the border and resolve differences amicably through dialogue and mutual respect. He also highlighted the importance of parliamentary diplomacy, stronger trade relations, and warmer people-to-people ties, expressing confidence that continued engagement through Parliamentary Friendship Groups and multilateral platforms such as BRICS would deepen mutual understanding.
Lok Sabha Speaker also met H.E. Dr. Ahmed Naderi, Member of the Presidium of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran. Recalling the historical ties between India and Iran and high-level engagements including their meeting in September 2026, Shri Birla emphasized the importance of peace and stability in West Asia. The leaders discussed taking forward Chabahar Port cooperation through joint efforts, and Dr. Naderi expressed gratitude for medicines, assistance, and other support extended by India to Iran. Both sides reaffirmed the importance of continued engagement to strengthen longstanding bilateral ties.

title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER INAUGURATES 12TH BRICS PARLIAMENTARY FORUM 2026; CALLS FOR EMPOWERING PARLIAMENTS TO ADVANCE PEOPLE-CENTRIC DEVELOPMENT
subtitle:
PRIME MINISTER SHRI NARENDRA MODI INTERACTS WITH PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATIONS FROM BRICS COUNTRIES

UNANIMOUS ADOPTION OF JOINT STATEMENT AT BRICS SUMMIT UNDER THE CHAIRMANSHIP OF PRIME MINISTER SHRI NARENDRA MODI WAS A LANDMARK ACHIEVEMENT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

TRUE MEASURE OF BRICS SUCCESS LIES IN TRANSLATING DIALOGUE INTO TANGIBLE OUTCOMES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

PARLIAMENTS CAN FOSTER MUTUAL TRUST, BRIDGE DIFFERENCES AND ADVANCE PEACEFUL RESOLUTION OF GLOBAL CHALLENGES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

VOICE OF THE GLOBAL SOUTH MUST FIND EXPRESSION IN CONCRETE POLICIES AND MEANINGFUL COOPERATION: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

HARNESS THE ASPIRATIONS OF YOUTH AND CHANNEL THEIR TALENTS INTO NATION-BUILDING: LOK SABHA SPEAKER URGES BRICS PARLIAMENTS

DEVELOPMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP ARE INSEPARABLE; COLLECTIVE ACTION ESSENTIAL FOR A SUSTAINABLE AND INCLUSIVE WORLD: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 3:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today inaugurated the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026 at the historic Samvidhan Sadan in the Parliament House Complex, New Delhi, calling upon the Parliaments of BRICS member and partner countries to strengthen their collective resolve towards people-centric development, global peace, sustainability and international cooperation. Emphasizing the transformative potential of parliamentary engagement, he underscored the need to harness the collective wisdom of nations to address shared challenges, deepen mutual understanding and bring meaningful, positive change to the lives of citizens.
Welcoming the parliamentary delegations from BRICS member and partner countries to India, Shri Birla observed that their presence reflected a shared commitment to dialogue, parliamentary cooperation, mutual respect and democratic values. He noted that notwithstanding their geographical, cultural, linguistic and social diversity, the countries were united by their faith in democratic ideals and a common sense of responsibility towards humanity. The true strength of BRICS, he said, lay in its ability to transform diversity into a source of strength, shared purpose and collective progress.
Describing the unanimous adoption of the Joint Statement at the BRICS Summit of Heads of State and Government held in New Delhi under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as a significant milestone, Shri Birla expressed his appreciation to the member countries. He emphasized that the real challenge now lay in translating the commitments embodied in the Joint Statement into tangible and lasting outcomes. Parliaments, through their legislative functions, budgetary processes, deliberations and oversight, could play a pivotal role in ensuring that these commitments translated into meaningful action and delivered tangible benefits to citizens.
Observing that the world was passing through a period of profound uncertainty, Shri Birla highlighted the mounting challenges posed by regional conflicts, wars, economic instability, trade tensions, terrorism and climate change. Their consequences, he noted, transcended national boundaries and called for a spirit of collective responsibility. In such a challenging global landscape, dialogue, diplomacy and cooperation assumed even greater significance. Parliaments, as vibrant expressions of the people's will, could serve as bridges of understanding, strengthen mutual confidence, ease international tensions and help advance peaceful and constructive responses to global challenges. Through parliamentary diplomacy, elected representatives could exchange perspectives, draw upon shared experiences, identify common interests and open new avenues for meaningful international cooperation.
Shri Birla observed that BRICS carried the significant responsibility of amplifying the voice of the Global South and advancing its aspirations on the world stage. He emphasized that this aspiration must move beyond the realm of dialogue and declarations to find concrete expression in responsive policies, practical cooperation and collective initiatives that improve people's lives. The strength of the grouping, he noted, would be reflected in its ability to transform shared aspirations into purposeful action and ensure that the concerns and priorities of developing nations received due consideration in global decision-making.
Highlighting the theme of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026, ‘Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development’, Shri Birla said it held particular relevance in the contemporary global context. The two-day Forum would provide an important platform for comprehensive deliberations on four interconnected pillars—resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability—each essential to strengthening democratic institutions and advancing inclusive development in an increasingly interconnected world.
Emphasizing the need for resilient parliamentary institutions, Shri Birla stated that BRICS countries must continually strengthen their legislative frameworks and institutional capacities to ensure continuity, accountability and effective democratic oversight, particularly in times of uncertainty and disruption. Parliaments, he observed, were living institutions that must evolve in step with the changing aspirations of the people. Their strength lay not merely in their constitutional authority but also in their ability to foster constructive dialogue, build consensus, uphold transparency and remain steadfastly accountable to the citizens they represent.
Underscoring the transformative role of innovation in parliamentary functioning, the Lok Sabha Speaker said that innovation extended beyond the adoption of new technologies to encompass fresh ideas, progressive practices and institutional reforms that made democratic institutions more effective, transparent, participatory and responsive. By embracing constructive change and strengthening institutional capabilities, parliaments could enhance the quality of deliberation, improve public engagement and respond more meaningfully to the evolving expectations of citizens.
Reflecting on the immense potential of parliamentary cooperation, Shri Birla observed that the diversity of BRICS countries was not a constraint but a valuable asset that could be harnessed for the common good. By sharing experiences, exchanging best practices and learning from one another's institutional strengths, their parliaments could collectively devise innovative responses to shared challenges. Such sustained engagement, he said, would help lay the foundations of a more equitable, inclusive and peaceful world.
He further emphasized that the essence of parliamentary diplomacy lay in fostering a culture of cooperation while fully respecting the sovereignty and distinctive perspectives of every nation. Differences in national circumstances need not impede the pursuit of common objectives; rather, constructive engagement could turn diverse viewpoints into opportunities for mutual learning and collective advancement. Calling for renewed commitment among BRICS member countries, Shri Birla urged them to transform experience into joint action, understanding into enduring trust, and dialogue into concrete and meaningful cooperation.
Turning to the imperative of sustainable development, Shri Birla observed that Indian philosophical thought regarded development and environmental preservation as complementary, mutually reinforcing pursuits. This holistic perspective, he said, offered an important guiding principle for the parliaments of BRICS countries. Development must not come at the cost of ecological balance; instead, policies for economic and social progress must be shaped by environmental responsibility, long-term sustainability and a deep commitment to safeguarding the interests of future generations. Collective action in this direction was indispensable to building a world that was prosperous, inclusive and environmentally secure.
Drawing attention to the hopes and aspirations of the younger generation, Shri Birla observed that today's youth were equipped with growing access to quality education and technological knowledge, alongside an immense desire to innovate, excel and contribute to society. Their aspirations must be met with meaningful opportunities, dignity and an enabling environment in which their talents could flourish. Parliaments, he emphasised, had a vital responsibility to listen to young voices, understand their hopes and concerns, and create pathways through which their energy, creativity and capabilities could be channelled into nation-building. Empowering young people, he said, was not merely an investment in their individual futures but a commitment to the collective destiny of nations.
Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of transforming BRICS into an ‘ecosystem of solutions’, the Lok Sabha Speaker underscored that the true measure of the Forum's success would lie not in the breadth of its discussions alone, but in the depth of its outcomes and the difference they made to people's lives. He called upon the parliaments of member countries to work towards a forward-looking agenda for a shared future, ensuring that dialogue culminated in action and cooperation yielded measurable results.
Shri Birla observed that although BRICS countries differed in their national circumstances, developmental priorities and perspectives, they were united by fundamental aspirations: peace, security, mutual respect, equal opportunities and a better quality of life for their citizens. These shared aspirations, he said, provided a strong foundation for deeper engagement and purposeful cooperation. The BRICS Parliamentary Forum must therefore emerge as a dynamic platform for building confidence, fostering understanding and advancing collective action in pursuit of these common goals.
Expressing confidence in the outcomes of the deliberations, Shri Birla said that the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum would further deepen the bonds of partnership among member countries and contribute meaningfully to the emergence of a more inclusive, peaceful and sustainable world. He expressed the hope that the discussions would impart fresh impetus to mutual trust and international cooperation, strengthen the collective commitment to people-centric development, and reinforce the shared determination of BRICS countries to translate common aspirations into enduring achievements.
On the occasion, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha Shri Harivansh also addressed the gathering. The Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha delivered the welcome address.

title: PM to inaugurate Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 on 27 October
subtitle:
Three-day Conclave to Bring Together Leading Scientists, Policymakers and Global Experts to Deliberate on Emerging Technologies and Innovation Priorities

ESTIC to Cover 12 Thematic Areas, including Artificial Intelligence, Biotechnology, Advanced Materials, Manufacturing, Healthcare, Energy, Climate and Ocean Sciences

A new initiative, Global Connect Networking Event, to Bring Over 300 Participants to Foster International Research Partnerships and Industry-Academia Collaboration
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 on 27 October 2026 at 5:30 PM at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
Scheduled from 27 to 29 October, the three-day Conclave will bring together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India's science, technology and innovation priorities.
Deliberations will span 12 thematic areas, including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances into practical applications.
The Conclave will also feature an extensive technology and innovation exhibition showcasing indigenous scientific achievements and emerging technologies. It will include around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which will highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors.
The Conclave will also use thematic videos, technology demonstrations, documentaries, informational kiosks and augmented and virtual reality experiences to enhance engagement with scientific developments and their real-world applications.
A new initiative, the Global Connect Networking Event, will bring together more than 300 invited participants from academia, research institutions and industry in India and abroad. It will provide a platform to explore international research partnerships, industry-academia collaboration and pathways for translating innovations from laboratories to markets.

title: Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh Delivers Welcome Address at the Inaugural Session of 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in Central Hall, Parliament of India, New Delhi
subtitle:
BRICS, representing around 49.5% of the global population, has become an effective multilateral platform, notes Shri Harivansh

The theme of the inaugural session "Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development”, both timely and relevant, says Shri Harivansh
date:

content:
The Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh today delivered the welcome address at the Inaugural Session of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum held in the historic Central Hall, Parliament of India, New Delhi.
Welcoming Hon'ble Speaker of Lok Sabha and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum, Shri Om Birla, Hon'ble Presiding Officers, Heads of Delegations from BRICS Member and Partner Countries, Excellencies, and Distinguished Delegates, Shri Harivansh stated that it is an honour to have all dignitaries and delegates present in the Central Hall. He highlighted that this historic hall has remained a silent yet living witness to India’s evolution as one of the world’s largest, most vibrant, and successful democracies. He described India as a timeless repository of knowledge, wisdom, and civilisational heritage, with its rich diversity of cultures, languages, landscapes, customs, and traditions, expressing confidence that delegates will carry back warm and lasting impressions of the country.
Highlighting the global role of the group, the Deputy Chairman noted that BRICS, representing around 49.5% of the global population, has become an effective multilateral platform for consultation and cooperation on issues having global as well as regional significance.
Shri Harivansh recalled that during the 2026 BRICS Presidency, India, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, introduced a transformative vision of a        “People-Centric” and "Humanity First" approach. Guided by this vision, the BRICS process has adopted the theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability." He added that Prime Minister Modi championed the expansion of the bloc, strengthening the voice and trust of the Global South. Furthermore, India’s presidency of the 18th BRICS Summit culminated in the adoption of the New Delhi Declaration, which advanced global governance reforms and fostered a more balanced, multipolar world order.
Reflecting on the theme of the Inaugural Session, "Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development," Shri Harivansh noted that it is both timely and relevant. He observed that citizens across the world expect Parliaments to respond effectively to emerging challenges, whether arising from economic uncertainties, technological transformation, climate change, public health emergencies, or social inequalities. Consequently, Parliaments must remain vigilant, responsive, dynamic, and future-ready in these fast-changing times. He stated that discussions in the Forum will provide an opportunity to exchange experiences, learn from one another, and identify parliamentary approaches that contribute meaningfully to improving the lives of people.
In conclusion, as the proceedings of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum commence, the Deputy Chairman extended sincere greetings to all delegates, wishing them productive discussions, successful outcomes, and a pleasant and memorable stay in India.

title: Cabinet Secretary chairs a meeting of National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) to review preparedness for the impending cyclone in Bay of Bengal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 3:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Cabinet Secretary, Dr. T. V. Somanathan today chaired a meeting of the National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) to review preparedness for the impending cyclone in the Bay of Bengal.
Director General, India Meteorological Department (IMD) briefed the Committee that the deep depression over East central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has moved nearly Westwards and intensified into cyclonic storm ‘ARNAB’ and lay centered at 0530 hrs IST of today over East central and adjoining West central Bay of Bengal about 590 km Northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands) 650 km East-Southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 730 km East-Southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 830 km East of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 910 km East of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh).
It is forecast to move west-northwestwards till 27th October and then northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast. It is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by forenoon of 28th October, 2026. Thereafter it is likely to affect districts in  Telangana, Southern Odisha, South & Central Chhattisgarh apart from Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
The Chief Secretaries/ Senior officials of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and the Union Territory of Puducherry apprised the Committee of the preparatory measures being undertaken by the State Governments/ local administration. It was informed that adequate shelters and evacuation arrangements have been made, and necessary NDRF and SDRF teams have been kept on standby. District Control Rooms have also been activated and they are monitoring the situation.
Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the Southwest and adjoining central Bay of Bengal, and along and off the coasts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Yanam (Puducherry) from 26th to 29th October. Those already at sea have returned.
Central Ministries/Departments attending the meeting informed the Committee that all Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are in place, necessary guidelines have been issued, and precautionary measures are being taken to minimise damage due to the impact of the cyclonic storm.
National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) informed that they have deployed teams, with additional teams on standby. Rescue and relief teams of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Indian Coast Guard, along with their ships and aircrafts, have been kept ready. Indian Coast Guard has so far shepherded multiple ships/boats to jetties/shore, and the remaining ships have been alerted to return to the coast. The Union Home Secretary informed the Committee that the Ministry of Home Affairs, NDMA and IMD are continuously monitoring the situation and coordinating with the Ministries/Departments, State Governments and other agencies.
Reviewing the preparedness measures of the Central agencies and the State Governments, Cabinet Secretary stressed that the objective should be to ensure zero loss of life and minimise damage to property and infrastructure. In the event of any damage, essential services should be restored in the shortest possible time. Cabinet Secretary also directed that in addition to Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and the Union Territory of Puducherry, since high rainfall was also expected in Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, they should be suitably alerted by MHA/IMD.
The meeting was attended by the Union Home Secretary;  the Chief Secretaries/ Senior officials of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha  and the Union Territory of Puducherry;  Secretaries in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, and Ministry of Power; Member and Head of Department and Secretary, NDMA; Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC); Director General, NDRF; Director General, IMD; Director General, Indian Coast Guard; Director General of Media and Communication, MHA; and senior officers of IMD and the Ministry of Home Affairs.

title: MDNIY Inaugurates Five-Day National Workshop on Patanjala Yoga Sutra
subtitle:
Workshop to Explore Vibhuti Pada Through a Systematic Study of Vyasa Bhashya


Experts Highlight Relevance of Patanjala Yoga Sutra in Understanding the Human Mind, Discipline and Consciousness
date:

                26 OCT 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY), Ministry of Ayush, today inaugurated a five-day National Workshop on “Patanjala Yoga Sutra: Vibhuti Pada (In the Light of Vyasa Bhashya)”. Scheduled from October 26 to 30, 2026, the workshop aims to deepen participants’ understanding of Vibhuti Pada through a systematic study of the Patanjala Yoga Sutra and its traditional interpretation.
Prof. Krishna Kant Sharma, former Professor, Department of Vedic Philosophy, Faculty of Sanskrit Vidya Dharma Vigyan (SVDV), Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi, participated as the subject expert and emphasised the importance of integrating classical wisdom with practical learning. He stated, “MDNIY is committed to imparting practical knowledge alongside a deeper understanding of the classical Yoga text Patanjala Yoga Sutra. The teachings of Maharishi Patanjali offer valuable insights into understanding and managing human suffering through Yoga.”
Dr. Jyoti Keswani, Director, MDNIY, highlighted the relevance of the Patanjala Yoga Sutra in personal development and the cultivation of discipline and awareness. She stated, “This classical text inspires us to become better human beings by cultivating discipline and awareness to manage the ego (Asmita). Each reading offers a new perspective. Vibhuti Pada, with its exposition of Siddhis, presents profound concepts that invite deeper philosophical inquiry and further scientific exploration. It encourages us to approach this traditional knowledge with an open mind, while recognising the importance of systematic research in understanding its significance and potential applications.”
Md. Taiyab Alam, Communication and Documentation Officer and DD (I/C), MDNIY, underscored the importance of applying the teachings of Yoga in everyday life. He stated, “The true essence of Yoga lies not in merely memorising the Yoga Sutras, but in integrating their wisdom into daily life. Vibhuti Pada, enriched by the philosophical depth of Vyasa Bhashya, offers profound insights into the discipline and purpose of Yoga. I am confident that this workshop will foster dialogue, learning and the dissemination of India’s classical Yoga heritage.”
Dr. I. N. Acharya, Programme Officer, MDNIY, discussed the contemporary relevance of the Patanjala Yoga Sutra, particularly in understanding and regulating the human mind. He stated, “In today's world, where information is increasingly accessible and life has become more complex, Patanjala Yoga Sutra offers valuable guidance for understanding and regulating the human mind while encouraging mindfulness and awareness.”
Vibhuti Pada, the third chapter of the Patanjala Yoga Sutra, explores advanced dimensions of Yogic practice, including Dharana, Dhyana and Samadhi, collectively known as Samyama. It also elaborates on various Siddhis (Yogic attainments), their implications and the importance of discernment in understanding their significance in the pursuit of spiritual progress.
The workshop provides an academic platform for an in-depth exploration of these concepts through a systematic study of the Sutras and the traditional commentary of Vyasa Bhashya. It also seeks to examine the philosophical foundations of Patanjala Yoga and the relevance of classical Yogic teachings in understanding higher stages of Yogic discipline and consciousness.
Dr. Indu Sharma, Assistant Professor, Yoga Education, MDNIY, is coordinating the workshop.
Through such academic initiatives, MDNIY continues to promote the systematic study of classical Yoga texts and strengthen understanding of India’s rich Yogic and philosophical heritage.

title: Department of Commerce Extends RELIEF Initiative under Export Promotion Mission Until March 31, 2027
subtitle: RELIEF Component II Offers 95% Risk Coverage to Encourage ECGC Cover for Export Shipments
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 1:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Commerce has extended the timelines under Component II of RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation), a time-bound intervention under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM), until March 31, 2027. The extension was notified vide Notification No. 37/2026-27 dated September 30, 2026, in view of continued geopolitical disruptions in West Asia and their impact on maritime logistics across the Gulf and adjoining regions.
Component II of the initiative aims to encourage exporters to obtain Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC) cover for upcoming shipments to specified regions by providing 95 per cent risk coverage. The benefit is available for Standalone Policies and Whole Turnover Policies obtained on or after March 16, 2026. Under this component, the premium payable by eligible exporters is protected against increases beyond pre-disruption levels during the eligible period. The covered cargo categories include Full Container Load (FCL), Less than Container Load (LCL) and refrigerated (reefer) containers, excluding energy shipments.
Exporters seeking coverage under the RELIEF initiative are required to submit claims and supporting documents through the ECGC customer portal at
www.ecgcltd.in
. Guidance on generating user IDs and passwords, completing exporter registration and submitting claims under the initiative is available through dedicated video tutorials on ECGC’s official YouTube channel, @ecgcltd7016.
Launched on March 19, 2026, RELIEF is a targeted intervention to support Indian exporters facing extraordinary freight cost escalation, higher insurance premia and war-related export risks arising from disruptions in the Gulf and the wider West Asian maritime corridor.
The extension of RELIEF underscores the Government’s commitment to strengthening export resilience, sustaining trade flows and supporting Indian exporters amid continuing geopolitical and maritime logistics uncertainties.

title: TRAI releases Recommendations on ‘Authorisation Framework for Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services’
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today released Recommendations on ‘Authorisation Framework for Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services’.
In view of the evolving broadcasting landscape, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) has sent a reference to TRAI, under Section 11(1)(a) of the TRAI Act 1997, on 15th December 2025, to examine and recommend a regulatory framework for Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television (FAST) Services ensuring parity, content accountability and consumer protection.
TRAI has examined such services and observed that several applications aggregate and distribute scheduled linear TV channels to consumers, either as pre-installed applications on TV sets and other devices; or as downloadable mobile/smart TV applications; or as web-based applications accessible through web browsers. Considering such wider scope of service provisioning through connected TVs, the services have been broadly referred to as ‘Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services’ including FAST Services.
Accordingly, the Authority on 6th April 2026, had issued a Consultation Paper titled ‘Formulation of a Regulatory Framework for Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services (Including Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television (FAST) Services)’ and solicited comments from stakeholders. In response, 207 comments and 11 counter-comments were received and uploaded on TRAI's website. As part of the consultation process, an Open House Discussion (OHD) was held on 10th June 2026, providing stakeholders an opportunity to present their views on the issues under consultation.
Based on the comments and counter-comments received from stakeholders, inputs gathered during the OHD, and its own analysis, the Authority has finalised its Recommendations on the ‘Authorisation Framework for Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services’. The recommendations seek to establish a light-touch and future-ready policy framework for Internet-based distribution of linear television channels, while promoting innovation, ease of doing business, consumer protection and regulatory certainty. These recommendations are built upon and complement the broader authorisation framework recommended by the Authority in its recommendations on ‘Framework for Service Authorisations for provision of Broadcasting Services under the Telecommunications Act, 2023’ issued on 21st February 2025.
Since ‘ALTD Service’ aggregates and distributes linear television channels over public Internet or other IP-based networks and provides consumers with a television viewing experience akin to conventional television distribution platforms across a variety of Internet-enabled devices, the Authority has recommended that ‘ALTD Service’ be introduced as a distinct sub-category under ‘Television Channel Distribution Services’ within the broadcasting authorisation framework under Section 3(1)(a) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023.  The recommendations further prescribe an authorisation framework, specifying the terms and conditions governing both the grant of authorisation and the provisioning of ‘ALTD Service’. The recommendations also provide obligations for key stakeholders like Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), Operating System (OS) providers and the broadcasters/content owners of the TV channels; measures for consumer protection; and inclusion of ALTD viewership in the television audience measurement framework, thereby covering all aspects of a linear television distribution services.
The salient points of the Recommendations are given below:
Introduction of ‘ALTD Service’ under Section 3(1)(a) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023.
‘ALTD Service’ is defined as aggregation of linear television channels that have been approved by the Central Government, including ‘Internet-native linear television channels’ (with approved name and logo), along with ALTD application provider’s own platform service channels, and its distribution to the users, with or without value-added services including on-demand audio-visual content, over public Internet or other IP-based networks through applications, websites or any other similar consumer interface, accessed through Internet-enabled devices.
Its scope covers development, deployment and management of such applications for users in India and excludes broadcaster-owned platforms distributing only their own channels or the channels of subsidiary/holding company; and live streams on social media intermediaries.
The terms and conditions governing ‘ALTD Service’ authorisation should be notified as Rules under Section 56 of the Telecommunications Act, 2023, and the authorisation, channel registration and reporting processes should be enabled through an online portal.
The Application Provider has been recommended as the primary entity responsible for obtaining authorisation for providing ‘ALTD Service’ and for complying with the applicable authorisation framework.
A light-touch authorisation framework has been recommended, with a national service area, an initial validity of 20 years renewable for successive periods of 10 years, an application processing fees of ₹10,000 and a one-time entry fee of ₹1 lakh, with no authorisation fee, bank guarantee or security deposit.
The detailed terms and conditions of grant of authorisation; and common and specific terms and conditions applicable to ‘ALTD Service’ have been recommended in alignment with TRAI's Recommendations on the authorisation framework for broadcasting services, with suitable modifications, to reflect the application-based and infrastructure-light nature of ‘ALTD Service’.
MIB should maintain a ‘Master ALTD app repository’. The OEMs (including television manufacturers) and the OS providers should ensure that only authorised ALTD applications are made available through their devices and application stores. They will be required to submit an annual compliance report to MIB in prescribed format.
In addition to existing permitted/authorised television channels, a framework has been recommended for simple registration of ‘Internet-native linear television channels’.
Authorised entity of ‘ALTD Service’ should distribute only the television channels holding valid permission/authorisation or registration from the Central Government.
The Application Provider should serve as the primary point of contact for consumer complaints and grievance redressal relating to ‘ALTD Service’.
Viewership of television channels distributed through ALTD applications should be integrated into the television audience measurement framework, and authorised ALTD application providers should be permitted to publish anonymised periodic viewership data in accordance with the TV Ratings Policy, 2026.
The recommendations aim to facilitate orderly growth of Internet-based linear television distribution services by providing an enabling authorisation framework.
The Recommendations have been placed on the TRAI's website (
www.trai.gov.in
). For any clarification/information, Dr. Deepali Sharma, Advisor (Broadcasting & Cable Services), TRAI, may be contacted at Telephone Number +91-11-20907774.

title: India Hosts 61st Meeting of International Committee of Legal Metrology in New Delhi
subtitle:
Secretary, Department of Consumer Affairs, Smt. Nidhi Khare, Highlights India’s Legal Metrology Reforms, Digital Transformation and International Cooperation

Initiatives such as e-Maap, Government Approved Test Centres and ‘One Nation, One Time’ Strengthen India’s Legal Metrology Ecosystem
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 7:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India is hosting the 61st Meeting of the International Committee of Legal Metrology (CIML) from 26 to 28 October 2026 at New Delhi. For the first time, India is hosting this prestigious international meeting of the International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML), bringing together delegates, senior officials and technical experts from across the world to advance cooperation in measurement standards, consumer protection and fair trade.
The programme commenced today with an international seminar on
“Evolutions in Legal Metrology”
, followed by the first session of the 61st CIML Meeting.
Dr. Bob Joseph Matthew, President of CIML, welcomed the international delegates and underscored the strategic importance of legal metrology in ensuring fair trade, protecting consumers and facilitating international cooperation.
Chairing the seminar, Ms. Renée Hansson, First Vice-President of CIML, Sweden, highlighted the evolving role of legal metrology in addressing digitalisation, emerging technologies and changing market requirements. She emphasised the need for harmonised measurement standards and closer cooperation among Member States.
Mr. Anthony Donellan, Director of the International Bureau of Legal Metrology (BIML), highlighted OIML’s efforts to develop internationally harmonised technical recommendations, facilitate the mutual acceptance of test results through the OIML Certification System (OIML-CS), and strengthen capacity building. He also highlighted emerging initiatives relating to machine-readable standards, artificial intelligence and digital transformation.
India’s Legal Metrology Reforms
Addressing the gathering, Smt. Nidhi Khare, Secretary, Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India, welcomed the international delegates and expressed pride in India hosting the CIML Meeting for the first time. She emphasised that accurate and internationally harmonised measurements are fundamental to fair trade, consumer confidence, industrial innovation and economic growth.
Highlighting India’s commitment to consumer protection alongside ease of doing business, the Secretary referred to the Jan Vishwas reforms of 2023 and 2026. These reforms have introduced measures such as decriminalisation of specified offences, improvement notices and graded penalties, promoting a more proportionate and business-friendly regulatory framework while retaining essential consumer safeguards.
She highlighted the expansion of Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) to augment verification capacity and the development of the e-Maap National Portal to provide integrated digital services in legal metrology. She also referred to India’s recognition as an OIML-CS Issuing Authority, an important step towards facilitating international acceptance of test results and supporting Indian manufacturers in accessing global markets.
The Secretary further highlighted the National Time Dissemination Project,
“One Nation, One Time”
, which aims to provide accurate, reliable and traceable Indian Standard Time across the country. The initiative is expected to strengthen time synchronisation in critical sectors, including banking, telecommunications, 5G networks, navigation, digital infrastructure and power systems.
Reaffirming India’s commitment to international cooperation, Smt. Khare stressed the importance of adopting emerging technologies and developing a transparent, efficient and future-ready legal metrology ecosystem.
Seminar Highlights Reforms and Emerging Technologies
During the seminar, Shri Ashutosh Agarwal, Director (Legal Metrology), Department of Consumer Affairs, delivered a presentation on
“Evolutions and Reforms in Legal Metrology in India”
. He traced the evolution of standardised weights and measures in India, from early civilisations to the modern legal metrology framework.
The presentation highlighted key initiatives aimed at simplifying compliance, strengthening verification infrastructure and modernising regulatory services, including GATCs, the e-Maap portal, regulation of packaged commodities, the National Time Dissemination Project, Regional Reference Standard Laboratories and the Indian Institute of Legal Metrology, Ranchi.
The international seminar featured presentations by experts from different countries on emerging challenges and opportunities in legal metrology. Discussions covered metrological requirements for electric vehicle charging equipment, mutual recognition of conformity assessment, digital transformation, stakeholder awareness and capacity building.
Experts also deliberated on OIML’s Smart Recommendations initiative, which aims to develop machine-readable technical standards, and explored the potential applications of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in measurement and verification systems. The discussions underscored the importance of harmonised standards in reducing technical barriers to trade and strengthening consumer confidence.
Further Deliberations on International Cooperation
The OIML Strategy Workshop will be held on 27 October 2026, followed by the second session of the CIML Meeting. The meeting will continue upto 28 October, 2026 with further deliberations on international legal metrology priorities and cooperation among Member States.
Hosting the 61st CIML Meeting reflects India’s growing role in international legal metrology and its commitment to accurate measurements, consumer protection, fair trade and globally harmonized standards.
The three-day programme includes a seminar on “Evolutions in Legal Metrology”, covering the digitalization of regulatory services, international recognition of instruments and e-learning. An OIML Strategy Workshop is scheduled for 27 October, followed by a visit to CSIR–National Physical Laboratory on 28 October. The visit will provide delegates an opportunity to learn about the institution’s role in maintaining India’s national measurement standards.
The deliberations reaffirm the shared commitment of India and the international legal metrology community to accurate measurement, transparent regulation, consumer confidence and smoother international trade. Through continued cooperation and the adoption of future-ready systems, the meeting seeks to strengthen legal metrology as an important enabler of innovation, economic growth and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: Raksha Mantri calls for ‘Aatmanirbharta 2.0’, next leap in defence self-reliance, at SWAVLAMBAN 2026
subtitle:
Cost-effective top-end technologies, robust R&D and resilient supply chains must for Viksit Bharat: Shri Rajnath Singh

Supply chain management a strategic imperative: RM calls for time-bound roadmap identifying critical tech, industries & resources

“Stronger industry-academia collaboration, greater encouragement in educational institutions and increased opportunities for youth key for fostering a deep-rooted culture of research & innovation”

“Need to develop technologies for civil & military applications and inter-service utilisation to promote jointness”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called for ‘Aatmanirbharta 2.0’ in the defence sector, with emphasis on the development of top-end, state-of-the-art technologies, strengthening Research & Development (R&D), and building resilient supply chains to reduce import dependence and achieve technological superiority, thereby contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. He was addressing the fifth edition of SWAVLAMBAN, the Indian Navy’s Naval Innovation and Indigenisation Seminar in New Delhi on October 26, 2026. He emphasised the need to build on the gains of the first phase of self-reliance achieved under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, ​​stating that defence innovators with futuristic vision and scientific discipline could play the role of ‘impact players’ in pursuing more challenging technological goals.
Highlighting the significant strides made by the nation towards Aatmanirbharta in defence over the last decade, Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that the progress achieved so far has created a strong foundation for the next phase, which must focus on advanced technologies and objectives that are considered difficult to achieve. He underlined the need to indigenously manufacture products that are cost-effective, operationally superior and globally competitive.
Raksha Mantri described supply chain management as not just a technical issue but a strategic imperative directly linked to national security. He called for a dynamic roadmap that sets clear timelines for achieving self-reliance in each item, identifies the technologies to be developed and the industries that will drive their innovation, and outlines the resources required to achieve these objectives. “Supply chain dependencies arise from a limited domestic availability of certain raw materials, such as rare earth elements, and the absence of specific technologies within the country. While some external dependencies may persist until viable alternatives are developed or domestic resources become available, there is a need to prioritise critical areas for indigenisation,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh underscored the need to remain prepared against potential disruptions in supply routes, stressing that the assessment of buffer stocks and domestic production capabilities must be carried out in advance rather than waiting for a crisis. He identified R&D as central to addressing these challenges. He exuded confidence in the ability of the nation’s talent pool to develop cutting-edge technologies indigenously with sustained focus and investment.
Raksha Mantri spoke of the inherent risks associated with research, and called for a change in attitude towards failure. He highlighted that even countries with advanced R&D ecosystems experience high failure rates, which are a natural part of the innovation process. “While this risk aversion is, in one sense, natural, it also presents an opportunity. Can we develop funding mechanisms capable of supporting high-risk, high-reward projects? Can we attract more private sector participation in R&D, given its greater propensity for risk-taking? We must seriously consider how to advance in two key areas: engaging the private sector and fostering low-cost technologies. The private sector possesses a greater capacity for taking risks, while low-cost technologies allow us to achieve significant results through smaller-scale experiments,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the R&D culture in countries such as Israel, South Korea and the United States where innovation, he said, is embraced as a way of life, with failure being viewed as an opportunity to learn. He stressed the need to foster a deep-rooted culture of research and innovation in India through stronger industry-academia collaboration, greater encouragement in educational institutions and increased opportunities for the youth to pursue careers in R&D.
Highlighting the contribution of iDEX in enabling start-ups and MSMEs to develop technologies that India previously imported, Raksha Mantri stated that over 4,000 proposals had been submitted against 229 challenges issued by the Indian Navy, reflecting the depth of Indian talent and the enthusiasm of entrepreneurs. Commending the progress made through iDEX, he said Indian start-ups and MSMEs have developed solutions in naval systems, sensors, communications and other critical areas by translating operational challenges into opportunities for innovation.
Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the demand for naval ships is steadily increasing in view of the evolving situation in the Indian Ocean Region, and since their construction is capital-intensive, there is a need to explore ways to reduce costs while expanding domestic production. He stated that the next phase of Aatmanirbharta must focus not only on the quantity of indigenous products but also on their quality, efficiency and affordability. He emphasised that self-reliance must strengthen national security as well as economic resilience.
“Our Government has ensured that a lack of funding does not become an obstacle to the aspirations of our talented youth. Naval contracts worth over Rs 1,900 crore demonstrate that our efforts are delivering tangible results. The steady progress of our Navy is a testament to this resolve… There is a need to address the remaining areas of import dependence, particularly Buyer Nominated Equipment, to further advance the Indian Navy’s journey towards self-reliance,” said Raksha Mantri.
For a broader approach to indigenisation, Shri Rajnath Singh called for the development of a ‘Dual Technology Roadmap’ to identify and prioritise technologies that can serve both civilian and military requirements. He stressed the need to expand efforts beyond existing Positive Indigenisation Lists and develop priority lists of technologies and products required for civil and military shipping. He also suggested identifying technologies that could be used across all three Services and the Indian Coast Guard, terming it as a technological application of inter-service jointness, which can serve as a significant milestone in the second phase of self-reliance.
Raksha Mantri appreciated the collaboration among the Defence Forces, industry and academic research institutions in addressing emerging challenges, including quantum technologies, artificial intelligence in warfighting and uncrewed systems. He underscored that developing such advanced capabilities requires perseverance, sustained collaboration and a clear focus on future operational requirements.
Speaking on the occasion, Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) Admiral Krishna Swaminathan highlighted the SWAVLAMBAN’s growth since 2022, with Navy-specific iDEX challenges increasing from 20 to 229, accounting for approximately 35% of all iDEX challenges across the defence sector. He noted that 41 Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) cases worth over Rs 3,500 crore have been accorded, while 25 contracts valued at over Rs 1,900 crore have been signed.
Emphasising the opportunities presented by advances in Artificial Intelligence, autonomous systems, robotics and quantum sensing, the CNS underscored the need to translate promising innovations into operational capabilities. He highlighted five key areas for accelerating capability development: ideation, prototyping, testing, contracting and induction, and life-cycle support. He called for stronger collaboration between the Indian Navy, industry, start-ups and MSMEs to accelerate the development and induction of indigenous technologies and build a self-reliant, future-ready defence ecosystem.
Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar stated that SWAVLAMBAN 5.0 marks another important milestone in the nation’s journey towards defence innovation and indigenisation, as it brings together all the stakeholders of the defence ecosystem on a common platform to deliberate on emerging technologies, address evolving operational requirements and explore new opportunities for indigenous capacity development. This year’s theme
‘Strength and Power through Innovation & Indigenisation’
, he added, reflects the growing importance of collaboration and technological advancements to build a strong and self-reliant defence ecosystem. He exhorted all the stakeholders to shift from competition to collaboration mode to contribute in further strengthening national security and nation-building.
The Secretary (Defence Production) appreciated the Indian Navy’s significant contribution in the success of the iDEX initiative. iDEX is translating indigenous innovations into tangible procurement outcomes and bolstering the Navy’s operational capabilities, he said.
Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Vice Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, CISC Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, Vice Chief of the Naval Staff Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar, Vice President, Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM) Shri Neeraj Gupta, serving and retired officials, industry & academia representatives and iDEX winners were present on the occasion.
Technology Exhibition
Raksha Mantri visited the technology exhibition with over 100 stalls by start-ups/MSMEs and interacted with innovators working on naval challenges  and problem statements. Start-ups/MSMEs engaged with naval users showcased niche technologies being progressed for operational capability development. Success stories section of the exhibition showcased developed products which are under induction by the Indian Navy.
Solutions in autonomous maritime platforms, quantum and AI in war-fighting, persistent surveillance, resilient navigation, advanced communications and counter-drone technologies illustrated the breadth of indigenous development. On the progress made since the launch of SWAVLAMBAN in 2022, Raksha Mantri stated that the platform has consistently contributed to meeting the operational requirements of the Indian Navy. He expressed confidence in the capability of Indian industry to develop reliable, high-end indigenous technologies, stating that the innovations showcased at the event reflected the country’s growing technological strength.
Publications and Recognition of Innovators
Shri Rajnath Singh released ‘Compendium of Technology Imperatives, Problems Statements and Future Concepts’ and ‘Swavlamban 5.0’ document providing industry visibility of naval priorities and development opportunities. He also felicitated eminent speakers of the seminar and iDEX innovators, recognising their contribution to India’s defence capabilities.
The event, organised by the Indian Navy in collaboration with the Defence Innovation Organisation and SIDM, is being held at Manekshaw Centre from October 26 to 27, 2026 on the theme ‘Strength and Power through Innovation and Indigenisation’. The seminar features deliberations on future and emerging technologies, including quantum technologies, Artificial Intelligence, autonomous systems and hypersonic technologies, with a focus on their potential applications in future warfare and naval operations.
Dedicated sessions are aimed at strengthening self-reliance and the iDEX ecosystem, building resilient domestic supply chains, promoting academic entrepreneurship and enabling start-ups to scale promising indigenous technologies. Engagements with investors and venture capitalists will provide opportunities to explore funding, scaling and commercialisation pathways for promising defence enterprises.

title: DAC clears capital acquisition proposals worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore for defence forces

content:
The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh on October  26, 2026, accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) i.e. in-principle administrative to various capital acquisition proposals of the Defence Forces at an estimated cost of about Rs 2,12,000 crore. For the Indian Army, approval was accorded for the procurement of High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System, Gun Shot Response System (GSRS), Light Multi Role Helicopters (LMRH), Very Short-Range Air Defence System (VSHORADS), Platform Based Counter Unmanned Aerial System (C-UAS), Unmanned Aerial System Brick Long Range, Surveillance UAV, Integrated Surveillance and Strike System and Long Range Kamikaze Drone System.
The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System will provide matching mobility and firepower to mechanised formations. The GSRS will serve as a force multiplier providing real-time situational awareness of the forces. The LMRH will be used by both the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force for Reconnaissance and Surveillance, Combat, Search and Rescue of troops, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief etc. The VSHORADS will engage new generation small size aerial threats, while C-UAS will enhance survivability of Tanks in the modern battlefield. The Surveillance and Drone Systems will enhance the surveillance and targeting capabilities of the Indian Army.
For the Indian Navy, approval was given for the procurement of Active Offboard Decoy System (AODS) and other major Naval platforms. The AODS will enhance the credibility of anti-missiles defence, especially against modern anti-ship missiles of adversaries. The indigenously designed and constructed major Naval platforms will possess modern-day warfare capabilities and enhance the combat capability of the Navy.
For the Indian Air Force, approval was accorded for the procurement of Helicopters, Air Defence Systems, Weapons and Mobile X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System to enhance the air defence and war fighting capabilities. The procurement of Special Utility Helicopters will help the Indian Air Force to meet the important air transport requirements. The X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System will provide high-resolution, localised weather surveillance in forward areas.
Out of the total AoNs accorded, approximately 82% of the procurements will be made from the Indian Industry.

title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Launches Capacity Building Programme for Medical and Allied Healthcare Professionals Engaged in Drug De-addiction Services
subtitle:
A Nasha Mukt Bharat by 2029 requires a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to address substance use disorders: Union Health Minister

Effective action against substance abuse requires synergy between healthcare, social welfare and law enforcement agencies: Shri Nadda

Programme aims to train 10,000 service providers by 2028-29 under the Vision Document on Narcotic Control: 2026-2029

Shri Nadda Launches Online Training Programmes for Medical and Allied Healthcare Professionals; Releases Second Edition of Management of Addictive Disorders: A Physician’s Manual
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 OCT 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda today launched the Capacity Building Training Programme for Medical and Allied Healthcare Professionals engaged in drug de-addiction services at Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi. The programme was launched in hybrid mode in the presence of the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and senior officers from the Ministries of Health and Family Welfare, Social Justice and Empowerment, and Home Affairs.
The programme aims to strengthen the capacity of healthcare professionals involved in the prevention, identification, assessment, treatment and management of substance use disorders across the country.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda congratulated the team for developing a comprehensive capacity-building programme with a structured implementation plan, incorporating online and offline training for doctors, medical officers, nurses, counsellors and other healthcare professionals. He appreciated the phased approach to training, which envisages collaboration among regional and national institutions, followed by the expansion of capacity-building activities across States and Union Territories.
The Union Health Minister reiterated the Government of India’s commitment, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, to achieving the goal of a Nasha Mukt Bharat by 2029. He emphasised that addressing substance abuse disorders requires a coordinated, whole-of-government approach, with different Ministries and departments working in synergy towards clearly defined objectives.
Shri Nadda observed that fragmented efforts and the functioning of different departments in silos had created gaps in coordination and service delivery. He noted that the
Vision Document on Narcotic Control: 2026–2029
, unveiled by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, represents a coordinated effort to address these gaps by defining the responsibilities and targets of various Ministries and departments. He stressed that effective implementation would require sustained inter-ministerial coordination and collective accountability.
Highlighting the role of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Shri Nadda stated that strengthening treatment services and building the capacity of healthcare professionals and de-addiction centres are central to the Ministry’s contribution to this national endeavour. He also underscored the importance of supporting de-addiction facilities under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment through appropriate training, institutional strengthening and adequate financial resources.
The Minister emphasised that the response to substance abuse disorders must extend beyond treatment to encompass prevention, enforcement and coordinated action against drug trafficking. He highlighted the importance of collaboration with law enforcement agencies, border-management authorities and other relevant stakeholders to address the challenge comprehensively. He encouraged healthcare professionals and participating institutions to share practical suggestions, including those requiring inter-departmental coordination, to strengthen implementation and address emerging challenges.
Concluding his address, Shri Nadda congratulated the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, and the participating institutions on the initiative. He expressed confidence that the capacity-building programme would strengthen the availability and quality of evidence-based treatment services and contribute to the collective national resolve of achieving a Nasha Mukt Bharat.
Speaking at the Occasion, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, quoted Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, emphasising that as India works towards the goal of a Viksit Bharat, it is essential to ensure that the country’s youth are physically healthy, mentally well, confident and free from the harmful effects of substance abuse. She highlighted that protecting young people from the dangers of drugs is crucial to nurturing a healthy, empowered and productive generation that can contribute meaningfully to the nation’s development.
She further underscored the importance of adopting a whole-of-government approach to address the challenge of substance abuse, stressing the need for coordinated efforts across Ministries, departments and institutions to strengthen prevention, awareness, treatment and rehabilitation services.
Dr. Anju Dhawan, Professor and Chief, National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, New Delhi, delivered a presentation outlining the implementation of the capacity-building programme for healthcare professionals engaged in the treatment of substance use disorders. She highlighted the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s mandate under the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026–2029), particularly the focus on strengthening treatment services and building the capacity of medical and paramedical personnel. She explained that the programme would be conducted through six institutions under the Drug De-Addiction Programme (DDAP), with NDDTC, AIIMS serving as the coordinating centre.
Dr. Dhawan elaborated on the training framework, which includes online live sessions for doctors, self-paced online modules for doctors, nurses and counsellors, and offline training for designated personnel. The curriculum covers different substances, including alcohol, cannabis, opioids, sleeping tablets and inhalants, along with the management of substance use disorders among specific groups, including women and adolescents.
During the event, Shri J.P. Nadda inaugurated the online live training programme for doctors and medical officers to be conducted by all six institutions under the Drug De-addiction Programme (DDAP). He also inaugurated the online self-paced training programme for nurses, Community Health Officers (CHOs) and Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs). The Union Health Minister, along with the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and other dignitaries, also released the second edition of ‘
Substance Use Disorder: Manual for Physicians
(Management of Addictive Disorders)’
.
About Drug De-Addiction Programme (DDAP)
The training programme will be conducted through six Central Government institutions under the Drug De-addiction Programme (DDAP): the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, New Delhi, located in Ghaziabad; the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru; the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh; the Central Institute of Psychiatry (CIP), Ranchi; Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi; and AIIMS Bhubaneswar. NDDTC, AIIMS will coordinate the overall implementation of the capacity-building initiative.
The programme will adopt a blended learning approach comprising online live training, in-person training and online self-paced courses. The online live training for doctors and medical officers will include weekly sessions over a 12-week period, combining theoretical lectures with clinical case discussions. The six designated institutions will conduct the sessions simultaneously, with a combined capacity of 300 participants per week. In-person training will be delivered through five-day programmes using a common curriculum developed by the participating institutions.
Self-paced online learning modules will also be made available for different categories of healthcare personnel. Doctors will have access to the NDDTC-developed NAAT online course, while the Addiction Rx application developed by NIMHANS will provide additional support for treatment-related prescribing. NIMHANS e-learning modules will be used for counsellors and psychologists, while NDDTC’s online course will support training for nurses, CHOs and ANMs. Certificates will be issued by the respective DDAP institutions upon completion of the training programmes.
The initiative will cover doctors, nurses, counsellors, psychologists, social workers and other medical and allied healthcare personnel involved in the delivery of substance use disorder treatment services. Participants will be nominated by State Governments through the National Health Mission (NHM), as well as by Central Government services, including the Armed Forces, Central Armed Police Forces and Railways. Personnel working in addiction treatment facilities funded by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will also be covered under the initiative.
More than 800 nominations have already been received through the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and DDAP institutions via the National Health Mission for online and offline training from various States. In addition, approximately 150 personnel from de-addiction centres supported by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment are expected to participate in offline training over the next two months. The training programme will leverage the existing clinical expertise, multidisciplinary faculty, academic infrastructure and e-learning resources of the six designated institutions.
The second edition of
Substance Use Disorder: Manual for Physicians (Management of Addictive Disorders)
, released during the event, provides practical guidance to physicians on the assessment and management of substance use disorders. First published in 2005, the manual has been extensively revised to incorporate significant advances in the scientific understanding of addiction, treatment approaches and service delivery over the past two decades, while retaining its emphasis on practical, evidence-based clinical care.
Designed for physicians working in both specialised addiction treatment facilities and general healthcare settings, the revised manual aims to strengthen their capacity to recognise, assess and manage substance use disorders with greater confidence and competence. It is expected to serve as a valuable resource in strengthening the delivery of evidence-based addiction treatment and improving access to quality care across the country.
Background
In June 2026, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah unveiled the Vision Document on Narcotic Control: 2026-2029, which outlines the Government of India’s strategy to tackle the entire drug trade ecosystem over the next three years. In line with the vision document, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has been entrusted with the responsibility of building the capacity of 10,000 service providers, including medical and allied healthcare personnel engaged in de-addiction services, by March 2029. The Ministry aims to train 2,000 service providers during the current financial year, followed by 3,000 in 2027-28 and 5,000 in 2028-29.
Through this initiative, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare seeks to expand access to competent, evidence-based and patient-centred addiction care, strengthen linkages across different levels of the healthcare system and contribute to the national commitment towards a Nasha Mukt Bharat.
The programme was attended by Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary and Managing Director, National Health Mission; Dr. Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services; Dr. (Ms.) Vinod Kotwal, Additional Secretary, MoHFW; and other senior officers of the Ministry.
Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, participated virtually, along with senior officials of the Ministries of Social Justice and Empowerment and Home Affairs, heads and faculty of the six designated DDAP institutions, State and Union Territory health officials, representatives of the Ministry of Education and Central Government healthcare organisations, and nominated doctors and allied healthcare professionals participating in the training programme.
